community.reason: Level 3: named community-investment programs with disclosed reach are present (Foundation grants of $5 million, the Docusign Impact volunteering program, and an employee match of $25 million supporting approximately 10,700 organizations), but these are not described as central to strategy, so level 4 does not apply.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 1, resting on general language only: the Human Capital section exceeds 150 words but offers only general statements ("every individual brings unique perspectives and experiences"), with no employee networks, accessibility features, multilingual services or programs for underserved groups. International operations and a "diverse customer base" do not count.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: very small businesses and individual entrepreneurs are customers of horizontal agreement software (with free and self-serve versions), but no specific enabling service aimed at founders' barriers is described.

notes: Final score = 0 + 18 + 4 + 3 = 25/100. The volunteering figure '140,000 hours' sits in the same paragraph as E2 but is split by a page break ('To date, our / Docusign, Inc. | 2026 Form 10-K | 11 / employees have volunteered'), so it was not used as a quoted indicator. Environmental nonprofit partnerships (Forest Stewardship Council, Wildlife Conservation Society) are mentioned without specifics and were not recorded separately. The developer ecosystem, Docusign Discover conference and App Center are commercial partner programs, not community education or creator enablement. Customer Success 'training' is customer onboarding and was not counted. International revenue and EU eIDAS offerings are market expansion, not cross-cultural activity. Item 7 excerpts repeat Item 1 content and add no new activities.
